parts.text: Which claim correctly describes the lines?

options.text: Each angle is a right angle, and that name alone settles the question.
The lines are perpendicular even if they stay apart and never meet.
The lines are perpendicular, because four equal angles at a meeting are each $90^{\circ}$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: The diagram shows lines $EF$ and $GH$ meeting at $P$. A right-angle mark sits at $P$, and all four angles at $P$ are equal.

part_answers.answer: Four equal angles at a meeting sum to $360^{\circ}$, so each is $90^{\circ}$ and the lines are perpendicular.

teacher.key_rationale: Four equal angles at P sum to 360°, so each is 90° and EF ⊥ GH. Stopping at the right-angle label or dropping the meeting condition misses that test.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle as intersecting lines EF and GH at P with a right-angle mark.
